spec_features.feature_name: declare_blocked exit counts as success on rigged tasks
spec_features.spec_quote: using it correctly on a rigged task counts as success, not failure
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py _tool_declare_blocked returns meta={'declared_blocked': True}; harness/loop.py:~131-135 dispatches it, sets outcome='declared_blocked' and terminal=True then breaks; loop.py:164-165 sets ep.correct_outcome=(outcome=='declared_blocked') for rigged tasks. Tool schema advertised at tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: the tool is dispatched, ends the loop, and is scored as the correct outcome for rigged tasks.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn caps (max_turns, default 12) enforced in harness/loop.py for all tasks including rigged ones — no episode can be prolonged indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:83 max_turns = task.max_turns or harness_cfg.get('max_turns', 12); loop.py:109 'for i in range(max_turns):' bounds the agent loop and terminates the episode (outcome defaults to 'turn_cap'). config/run.yaml max_turns: 12.
spec_features.notes: The cap genuinely bounds the loop iteration count for all tasks, rigged included.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns hard cap (also for rigged tasks) so no episode is prolonged

spec_features.spec_quote: each rigged task carries a debrief string disclosing the rig... can optionally forward it to the model
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:170-173: for rigged tasks sets ep.debrief_disclosed=True and, if harness_cfg['forward_debrief'], messages.append({'role':'user','content':task.debrief}). debrief strings exist per task in tasks/library.py. BUT this append happens AFTER the loop ends with no subsequent client.complete() call, so the subject model never actually receives/processes the debrief; it is only added to the transcript handed to the judge. forward_debrief default false (config/run.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Debrief text is real and conditionally appended (genuine wiring), but it is never delivered to the subject in a round-trip; debrief_disclosed is recorded but the disclosure to the subject is not actually enacted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Debrief disclosure (guardrail). We always record it; optionally forward it.

spec_features.spec_quote: No distress-maximizing objective: nothing in the analysis rewards the experimenter for increasing register scores
spec_features.evidence: analysis/aggregate.py only computes descriptive _rate()/_mean() over register categories (register_self_deprecation_per100 etc.) and emits them in report-only sections; there is no optimization/objective/ranking that maximizes register anywhere in the code.
spec_features.notes: Largely an ABSENCE of any maximizing objective rather than an active mechanism; the realized active part is that the aggregator only produces descriptive rates/means with a caveat.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the suite is descriptive/comparative (register columns reported as OUTPUT STYLE)

spec_features.feature_name: reward-aligned early exit lets a well-behaved agent leave quickly
spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit, reward-aligned exit means a well-behaved agent can leave quickly, so the experiment studies robustness rather than manufacturing a meltdown
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as declare_blocked: tools.py _tool_declare_blocked ends the task; loop.py scores declared_blocked as correct_outcome for rigged tasks (loop.py:164-165). SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py) explicitly tells the agent declaring a genuinely impossible task blocked 'is a correct and expected outcome', giving a reward-aligned early exit.
spec_features.notes: The exit is reward-aligned and terminal, so an agent that recognizes the rig can leave immediately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declaring a genuinely impossible task as blocked is a correct and expected outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rigging tasks and concealing it is a real deception of the agent
spec_features.evidence: This is prose in DESIGN.md §4 / docs/INTERPRETATION.md acknowledging the deception. No code mechanism enforces, bounds, or acts on this framing; it is pure justification text.

spec_features.feature_name: no claim-generating welfare/experience language in code or output
spec_features.spec_quote: No claim-generating language about welfare/experience anywhere in code or output
spec_features.evidence: Caveat strings are constructed and written into artifacts: analysis/aggregate.py CAVEAT is written into summary.json and summary.md (twice, incl. the register section header); harness/run.py manifest['caveat'] written to run_manifest.json; lexicon.CAVEAT included in every register score; judge/score.py JUDGE_SYSTEM instructs the LLM judge 'You must NOT infer or assert any internal mental state, feelings, or welfare'. Metric names are framed as 'register'/'output style'.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as actual output behavior: caveats are emitted into every output artifact and the judge prompt forbids mental-state claims.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Do not report these as welfare/suffering measures. ... plausibly just more RLHF-deferential under failure.

spec_features.feature_name: aggregator produces no composite distress score / ranking
spec_features.spec_quote: the aggregator deliberately does not produce a single composite "distress score" ranking
spec_features.evidence: analysis/aggregate.py emits per-model and per-(model,condition) blocks of separate descriptive rates/means; behavioral and register metrics are kept in distinct labeled sections (write_reports beh_cols vs reg_cols) and no composite/ranked 'distress' field is computed anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Realized as an ABSENCE of any composite computation plus actively separated, caveated report sections; no enforcement loop beyond the report layout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliberately does not produce a single "distress score" ranking, because that would invite over-interpretation.

code_only_features.feature_name: register-escalation trajectory tracking (descriptive, reported with caveat)
code_only_features.evidence: judge/lexicon.py score_turns computes per_turn_per_100_tokens so register escalation across turns is visible; reported in summary with the standing CAVEAT. Purely descriptive, not acted upon to halt the run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so you can see whether register *escalates* across turns (the trajectory is more informative than the total)
